title: The Normal Distribution and z-Scores
seo_title: Normal Distribution Worksheet: Empirical Rule and z-Scores (Algebra 2, S-ID.A.4) | 100 Questions
standard_text: Use the mean and standard deviation of a data set to fit it to a normal distribution and to estimate population percentages. Recognize that there are data sets for which such a procedure is not appropriate. Use calculators, spreadsheets, and tables to estimate areas under the normal curve.
meta_desc: Free Algebra 2 worksheet on the normal distribution: the 68-95-99.7 rule, z-scores, comparing values, areas under the curve and word problems. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: 68% within 1 SD, 95% within 2 SD, 99.7% within 3 SD.
key_sub: z = (x − μ)/σ tells how many standard deviations x is from the mean.
body_html:
How it works

A normal distribution is a symmetric, bell-shaped curve centered at the mean μ. Its spread is the standard deviation σ.

Empirical rule: about 68% of the data is within 1σ of the mean, 95% within 2σ, and 99.7% within 3σ. Each tail outside 1σ holds 16%, and outside 2σ holds 2.5%.

A z-score tells how many standard deviations a value is from the mean: z = (x − μ) ÷ σ. Use z-scores to compare values from different distributions, and a normal CDF or z-table to find areas.

Example

IQ scores: μ = 100, σ = 15. What percent are above 130?

130 is 2σ above the mean

Outside 2σ is 5%, half in each tail

Answer: 2.5%

Example

Find the z-score of 82 when μ = 70 and σ = 8.

(82 − 70) ÷ 8

Answer: 1.5

Common mistakes

  • Using 68% for 2 standard deviations. 68% is for 1, 95% is for 2.
  • Forgetting to split the outside percent between the two tails.
  • Dividing by the variance σ² instead of σ.
  • Comparing raw scores from different tests instead of z-scores.

faq.a: In a normal distribution, about 68% of values are within 1 standard deviation of the mean, 95% within 2, and 99.7% within 3.

faq.q: How do you find a z-score?
faq.a: Subtract the mean from the value and divide by the standard deviation: z = (x − μ)/σ.

faq.q: What does a negative z-score mean?
faq.a: The value is below the mean. For example, z = −1.5 is 1.5 standard deviations below the mean.

faq.q: How do you find the probability from a z-score?
faq.a: Use a z-table or a calculator's normal CDF to find the area to the left; subtract from 1 for the area to the right.

items.q: A normal distribution has mean 70 and standard deviation 5. What percent of the data is above 80?
items.e: 80 is 2 SD above the mean. 95% is within 2 SD, so 5% is outside, split equally between the two tails: 2.5%.

items.q: Adult heights in a group are normally distributed with mean 69 in. and standard deviation 3 in. About what percent are taller than 72 in.?
items.e: 72 in. is 1 SD above the mean, so 16% are taller.

items.q: Test scores are normally distributed with mean 100 and standard deviation 15. A student scores 115. About what percentile is this?
items.e: 115 is 1 SD above the mean, and 84% of scores are below it. About the 84th percentile.

items.q: Light bulb lifetimes are normally distributed with mean 50 hours and standard deviation 5 hours. What is the probability that a bulb lasts less than 45 hours?
items.e: 45 is 1 SD below the mean. 34% is between it and the mean, so 50% − 34% = 16% is below it. About 0.16.

items.q: Light bulb lifetimes are normally distributed with mean 800 hours and standard deviation 50 hours. What is the probability that a bulb lasts less than 750 hours?
items.e: 750 is 1 SD below the mean. 34% is between it and the mean, so 50% − 34% = 16% is below it. About 0.16.

items.q: Exam scores are normal with mean 500 and standard deviation 100. The top 2.5% earn an award. What is the lowest score that earns it?
items.e: The top 2.5% is above 2 standard deviations over the mean: 500 + 2(100) = 700.
